FINDING_ID: F001 | SEVERITY: 0.98 | FLAW_CLASS: 5 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.95  
DESCRIPTION: At [bench/dynamic_management.py:3542](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3542) `process_round()` records `round_idx = self.fsm.current_round` before the FSM advances, and [bench/dynamic_management.py:1236](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1236) leaves BLIND -> SYNTH at round `0`; direct execution produced `round_results idx [0, 0]` and only one convergence round key, so the SYNTH phase overwrites BLIND-phase evidence.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Give BLIND and SYNTH distinct round indices, or make SYNTH non-recordable; at minimum, advance the round counter before persisting SYNTH outputs and reject duplicate round keys.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002 | SEVERITY: 0.94 | FLAW_CLASS: 5 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.86  
DESCRIPTION: [bench/dynamic_management.py:1641](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1641), [bench/dynamic_management.py:1656](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1656), and [bench/dynamic_management.py:1711](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1711) make an all-empty run converge with `kappa=1.0`; direct execution after three empty rounds returned `converged True`, contradicting the module’s own “not converged unless null_expected” comment.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an explicit empty-findings guard in `converged()`/`kappa()` so an empty corpus does not count as convergence unless the caller opts into that convention.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003 | SEVERITY: 0.89 | FLAW_CLASS: 5 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.84  
DESCRIPTION: The docstring at [bench/dynamic_management.py:1344](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1344) says equivalence requires same `flaw_class`, but [bench/dynamic_management.py:1459](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1459) and [bench/dynamic_management.py:1557](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1557) still merge cross-class findings if text similarity is high; direct execution merged class `1` and class `2` findings into one class and mislabeled the cluster as flaw class `1`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Enforce `flaw_class` equality inside `_compute_equivalence_classes()` or `_finding_similarity()`, and reject mixed-class clusters instead of inheriting `members[0].flaw_class`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004 | SEVERITY: 0.88 | FLAW_CLASS: 5 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.88  
DESCRIPTION: Role reassignment at [bench/dynamic_management.py:499](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L499) reads `self._models` only, while live feedback is maintained separately at [bench/dynamic_management.py:3880](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3880); after forcing live COL scores to favor `m3` (`1.0`) over `m2` (`0.0`), `reassign()` still kept `m2` as COL.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Reassign roles from live `ModelSpec` data, not frozen initial specs, or inject `get_live_models()` output into `RoleAssignment.reassign()`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005 | SEVERITY: 0.86 | FLAW_CLASS: 5 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.90  
DESCRIPTION: The stop contract claims an ascending-abstraction guard is conjunctive, but [bench/dynamic_management.py:2201](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2201) never calls `_abstraction_dropping()` from [bench/dynamic_management.py:2187](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2187); direct execution returned `stop=True` at round 2 while `abstraction_drop=False`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Encode the documented conjunctive rule directly in `stop()`, or remove the guard from the API/docs if it is intentionally not part of stopping logic.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006 | SEVERITY: 0.86 | FLAW_CLASS: 5 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.83  
DESCRIPTION: [bench/dynamic_management.py:947](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L947) returns infeasible allocations as normal results and only emits a warning; direct execution with a 200-token task on a 100-token model returned `matrix [[1]]`, load `200`, and `balanced True`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make infeasibility explicit in the return type or raise on HARD-constraint violations; do not present overloaded plans as successful allocations.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F007 | SEVERITY: 0.82 | FLAW_CLASS: 2 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.87  
DESCRIPTION: `process_round()` at [bench/dynamic_management.py:3557](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3557) inspects only models present in `responses`, so missing dispatched models are never marked EMPTY/TIMEOUT; direct execution with three active models and one response left `m2` and `m3` active and absent from `failures`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass the expected responder set or allocation into `process_round()` and synthesize failures for missing responses before convergence/stop logic runs.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F008 | SEVERITY: 0.81 | FLAW_CLASS: 5 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79  
DESCRIPTION: Critical-task redundancy is computed against total model count at [bench/dynamic_management.py:780](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L780), but PM is inadmissible for normal tasks at [bench/dynamic_management.py:761](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L761); with three models and a critical task, direct execution produced target `3`, admissibility `[[0,1,1]]`, allocation `[[0,1,1]]`, and `feasible (True, [])`, so the redundancy contract is silently unmet.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute redundancy targets from admissible active workers and add an explicit feasibility check for unmet redundancy targets.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F009 | SEVERITY: 0.78 | FLAW_CLASS: 5 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: The manager reports and health-checks raw system `marginal_value()` from [bench/dynamic_management.py:3623](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3623), while the actual stop decision at [bench/dynamic_management.py:2201](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2201) uses smoothed/per-model mu; direct execution gave `reported_mu 0.3` but `smoothed_mu = aggregate_per_model_mu = 0.9`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Feed the same mu variant into `RoundResult`, events, and `DetectorHealthMonitor` that `stop()` actually uses, or expose both metrics with distinct names and semantics.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F010 | SEVERITY: 0.75 | FLAW_CLASS: 5 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: Adaptive `tau_sim` changes at [bench/dynamic_management.py:3992](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3992) do not invalidate cached equivalence classes built at [bench/dynamic_management.py:1525](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1525); direct execution kept `len(get_round_classes(0)) == 2` after lowering `tau_sim` from `0.8` to `0.3`, even though the pair similarity was `0.6033`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Clear `_round_classes` and `_cumulative_classes` whenever similarity parameters change, or rebuild the detector from scratch after immune adaptation.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F011 | SEVERITY: 0.73 | FLAW_CLASS: 2 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: `check_dispatch_feasibility()` at [bench/dynamic_management.py:3478](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3478) emits `DISPATCH_BLOCKED` but never calls the tracking hook at [bench/dynamic_management.py:4079](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4079); direct execution blocked a model and left `_dispatch_blocks` empty, so dispatch-health diagnosis has no input data.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Record blocks inside `check_dispatch_feasibility()` and record later success automatically when a previously blocked model completes a round.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F012 | SEVERITY: 0.69 | FLAW_CLASS: 5 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70  
DESCRIPTION: The dispatch auto-fix path is broken by a string mismatch: [bench/dynamic_management.py:2628](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2628) emits `"Dispatch false positive..."`, but [bench/dynamic_management.py:4018](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4018) looks for `"false_positive"`; direct execution of `apply_diagnosis()` returned `None` and left `pre_decompose_models` unchanged.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Match on structured fields (`detector`, explicit pathology code) rather than parsing free text, or normalize both sides to the same token convention.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F013 | SEVERITY: 0.64 | FLAW_CLASS: 2 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.48  
DESCRIPTION: FORMAT failures are emitted as `MALFORMED` at [bench/dynamic_management.py:2831](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2831) even though `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION` exists at [bench/dynamic_management.py:3206](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3206); direct execution returned `FailureType.FORMAT` but the event stream contained `['MALFORMED']`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit `FORMAT_VIOLATION` for parseable-but-noncompliant responses and keep MALFORMED reserved for unparseable payloads.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F014 | SEVERITY: 0.58 | FLAW_CLASS: 6 | ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: The FSM mishandles `max_rounds=1`: [bench/dynamic_management.py:1165](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1165) sets `max_round_idx = 0`, but [bench/dynamic_management.py:1239](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1239) still allows `SYNTH -> ROUND_1`; direct execution showed `BLIND -> SYNTH` with valid SYNTH events including `COMPLETE`, which can create a round beyond the configured maximum.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `max_rounds >= 2` for this FSM shape, or special-case `max_rounds=1` so SYNTH transitions only to TERMINAL outcomes.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
